introduces.gloss: a number that goes into the machine
the setting of a dial: how much its input counts
the output we want for these inputs
inputs, weights, a sum, a valve, an output

sentences: {machine}This is a machine that turns numbers into a number.
{tubes}Two numbers go in on the left, held as light in these glass tubes.
{input}Each one is called an input.|
{x1}This one holds two. {x2}This one holds one.
{dials}Each input flows through a dial.
{w1up}Turn a dial up, and its input counts for more.
{w2down}Turn it below zero, and its input pulls the total down.
{weight}The setting of a dial is called a weight.|
{chamber}In this chamber, everything that flows in is added up.
{valve}Then a one way valve. Below zero, nothing passes.
{gauge}What comes out, on this gauge, {output}is the output.|
{target}The brass mark is the output we want. The target.|
{recap}Inputs, weights, a sum, a valve, an output.
{neuron}This whole instrument is one neuron.|
{pull}Wire many neurons together, so the outputs of some become the inputs of others, {network}and you have a neural network.|
{billions}Large networks have billions of dials.
{tuned}Nobody sets them by hand. They are tuned, until the outputs meet their targets.
Your turn. Take the first dial, and turn it two clicks to the right.
The needle rose. The first input now counts.
Now turn the second dial, until the needle sits on the brass mark.
On the mark. That is tuning. Dials set, so the output meets the target.
One example is easy. Here are four, each with its own target.
A tuner that turns the dials by itself will race you, one small step every second.
The ember columns show how far the needles are from their marks. Pull the lever to start.
All four needles on their marks, ahead of the tuner.
The tuner got there first. Each step, it turns every dial a little, toward a smaller miss.
The second dial moves needles two and four the most.
To tune itself, a network needs one number that says how wrong it is.
That number is the next instrument.
